clue.text: Expert lawmen thus called in for murders

indicators.note: the lawmen and thus are summoned inside, so they go within the expert word

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast with expert knowledge
MP stands for military police, soldiers who enforce the law
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: Specialist detectives are summoned to investigate a killing spree.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump off is slang for killing someone, so the phrase works as a verb for murders.

clue.text: Pack and be first to dress

indicators.note: the be piece comes first, ahead of the pack piece

parts.note: taken as written
a deck is a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pack a bag and be the first to get dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedeck is to adorn or dress something up with decorations.

clue.text: Head of maths, working with computers, needs men for in-class help

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word maths is used

parts.note: on means operating, working
IT is information technology
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A head of department needs more staff to help in computer classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor is a pupil given duties to help the teacher in a class.

clue.text: I'm unable to support unlimited provision for beggar

indicators.note: in a down clue the I'm unable piece holds up the other from below
the provision word loses its limit, its final letter

parts.note: a supply is a provision of goods
I can't means I am unable

explanation.surface: Someone protests they cannot keep giving endless handouts to a beggar.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplicant is one who begs humbly, so a beggar.

clue.text: Traveller, having to pay full amount for ticket, turned green

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay all of it
a pass is a ticket permitting entry or travel

indicators.note: the letters of green are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller goes pale after being forced to pay full fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot passenger is someone travelling on a ferry without a vehicle.

clue.text: Scottish bishop appears formal to us

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper, formal in manner
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish churchman comes across as rather stiff to those meeting him.
explanation.walkthrough: The Primus is the presiding bishop of the Scottish Episcopal Church; 'appears' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Primus is the title of the elected senior bishop in the Scottish Episcopal Church.

clue.text: Take top off instant cereal

indicators.note: the first letter, the top in a down clue, is removed

parts.note: a trice is an instant, as in 'in a trice'

explanation.surface: Instructions for opening a packet of instant breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain example: rice is one of the grain crops classed as cereals, alongside wheat and barley.

clue.text: Superior position on board isn't commonly held by cleaner

indicators.note: the colloquial word sits inside the cleaner piece

parts.note: a mop is a cleaning tool
ain't is a nonstandard, common form of isn't

explanation.surface: A cleaner is rarely given a top seat on the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a boardroom, but it means aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The maintop is the platform at the head of a ship's mainmast, a high position on board.

clue.text: Comparatively hot and humid in various emirates

indicators.note: the letters of emirates appear in a varied arrangement

explanation.surface: Weather reports compare the heat and humidity across the Gulf states.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamier is the comparative of steamy, meaning hot and humid.

clue.text: Teacher identified cheat at end of examination

parts.note: to do someone is slang for swindling them

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word examination is wanted

explanation.surface: A teacher catches a pupil cheating at the end of an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge.

clue.text: I've joined search for gold, as anticipated

indicators.note: the I've piece is attached to the search-for-gold piece, after it

parts.note: to prospect is to search for gold or other minerals
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man signs up for the gold rush, just as everyone expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospective means expected or likely to happen, which is what is anticipated.

clue.text: Cinema employee, as forecast, is put on short time

indicators.note: in a down clue the is piece is placed above the short time piece

parts.note: a projection is a forecast
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: As predicted, a cinema worker has their hours cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short time' suggests reduced working hours, but it just means T.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectionist runs the film projector in a cinema.

clue.text: It'll cause a bit of a shock on Jersey and Guernsey

definitions.text: It'll cause a bit of a shock on Jersey and Guernsey

parts.words: It'll cause a bit of a shock on Jersey and Guernsey
parts.note: Jersey and Guernsey read as the Channel Islands but are breeds of dairy cow, and a farm tool gives livestock a small electric jolt

explanation.surface: Some event will rock the Channel Islands of Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey and Guernsey look like the Channel Islands, but here they are breeds of cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle prod is a stick that gives cows a mild electric shock to move them along.

clue.text: One entry in ledger book, or a couple

definitions.meaning: a single line or listed article in an account
two people known to be romantically together, as in gossip

explanation.surface: An accountant explains that a line in the books may stand alone or be one of a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single listed entry, and two people dating are called an item.

clue.text: Dope penetrating least familiar area of the Amazon?

indicators.note: the dope piece pushes into the least familiar piece

parts.note: rarest means least common, least familiar
dope is slang for information

explanation.surface: Drugs are found deep in the most remote parts of the jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: Much of the Amazon basin is tropical rainforest; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Dogs, and where they chase hares?

definitions.meaning: to dog someone is to follow them closely, as a pursuer does
greyhounds race round courses chasing a mechanical hare

explanation.surface: A question about where greyhounds run after hares.
explanation.definitionFit: To track is to dog someone, and greyhound racing takes place on tracks.

clue.text: Model learner allowed in gym after test

indicators.note: the gym piece comes after the test piece in the answer

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: the learner is let into the gym piece, so it sits inside

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An ideal student is admitted to the gymnasium after passing a test.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a model to be followed or copied.

clue.text: Person most likely to become puzzle expert?

definitions.text: Person most likely to become puzzle expert?

parts.words: Person most likely to become puzzle expert?
parts.note: reads like a quiz about a crossword whizz, but describes a candidate thought likely to be picked, as for a team

explanation.surface: Who will most probably turn into a crossword champion?
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, the word means a person likely to be chosen or to succeed.

clue.text: One way in France to secure regular income

indicators.note: the French way holds the regular piece inside it

parts.note: rue is the French word for a street
even means steady, regular

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a way to earn a steady income in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income, especially money coming into a business or state.

clue.text: See a wild animal and scarper!

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see
a moose is a large wild deer

explanation.surface: A warning to spot a wild beast and run away.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is slang for leaving hurriedly, like the British scarper.

clue.text: King and Jack, perhaps? Two different cards

parts.note: a ten and an ace are two different playing cards
a ten and an ace are two different playing cards

explanation.surface: A card player names two court cards, then two other cards.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a tenace is a holding of two cards separated by a missing one, like king and jack with the queen absent.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenace in bridge is two high cards with a gap between them, and king with jack is an example.

clue.text: Idle hick briefly stirred by this social gathering

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up and mixed into a new order
the word hick is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A lazy country bumpkin is roused by a lively party.
explanation.walkthrough: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish gathering with folk music and dancing; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceilidh is a social event with traditional music and dancing.

clue.text: Rock legend, ultimately high on drugs

parts.note: a stone is a piece of rock

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word legend is taken

explanation.surface: A rock star of legend ends up drugged out.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned is slang for intoxicated by drugs.

clue.text: Fail to move quickly

definitions.meaning: to flop badly, as a play does at the box office
to go very fast, as in tearing along a road

explanation.surface: A warning that failing to hurry will cost you.
explanation.definitionFit: To bomb means both to flop completely and, informally, to speed along.

clue.text: Crop expert's short, gastronomic, concoction

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture made up from ingredients, so the letters are remixed
the word is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A food scientist cooks up a brief, gourmet dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An agronomist is a scientist who studies soil and crop production.

clue.text: Challenge one abandoning worship

indicators.note: the one piece is left out of the worship word

parts.note: to deify is to worship as a god
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone challenges a believer to give up religion.
explanation.definitionFit: To defy is to challenge or openly resist.

clue.text: Noisily expresses contempt for sailors making cross Channel trip?

indicators.note: the words are said out loud, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: boos crews: jeers at ship's crews

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at sailors who are crossing the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: A booze cruise is a British day trip by ferry to France to buy cheap alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A booze cruise is a ferry trip across the Channel to stock up on cheaper drink in France.

clue.text: Somewhere to stay, visiting Minnesota

indicators.note: the answer pays a call inside the word Minnesota

explanation.surface: A traveller looks for a room while in Minnesota.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub or small hotel offering lodging.

clue.text: Woman's extremely lucky to get new man?

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, stands for any woman

indicators.note: only the outer letters of the word lucky are taken

explanation.surface: A woman is fortunate to land a fresh boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Evelyn, though usually a woman's name now, is also a man's name (Evelyn Waugh).
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn is a given name borne by men, such as the novelist Evelyn Waugh.

clue.text: Bound to keep bird caught in outbuilding

indicators.note: the bird and caught go inside the outbuilding

parts.note: a shed is a small outbuilding
a tit is a small songbird
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A captured bird must be kept in a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound in the sense of a book's pages fastened together by sewing.
